 KEY TAKEAWAYS: 
 Krunal Pandya and Abbas Afridi again skipped the handshake at the Hong Kong Sixes toss.
 Afridi hit five sixes off Pandya's opening over as Pakistan won by four wickets.
 India collapsed to 88 for five, which was the lowest total of the day.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement India vs Pakistan Hong Kong Sixes 2026: Krunal Pandya avoids handshake at toss as PAK beat IND by four wickets
 India and Pakistan avoided handshakes yet again when they met at the Hong Kong Sixes 2026 on Friday, and the familiar scene played out on a day when Pakistan also beat their rivals comfortably on the field.
 The two captains, Krunal Pandya and Abbas Afridi, did not exchange any greeting at the toss, which Pakistan won before choosing to bowl first.
 The same thing is believed to have happened after the game, although there is no footage to confirm it, since the broadcast feed was cut immediately after Pakistan's winning hit. Viewers were therefore left without any images of the closing moments, and the question of whether the sides greeted each other remains unanswered by the cameras.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The refusal has now become a regular feature of India-Pakistan meetings, and it didn't change even though the match took place in a light-hearted six-a-side format.
 Abbas Afridi hits five sixes in one over off Krunal Pandya
 Pandya took the new ball himself and began in the worst possible way, because Afridi struck him for six off each of the first four balls, and then followed it with a fifth. The over produced 31 runs as Pakistan set the tone early. 
 Natarajan was next in line to suffer, and he conceded a no-look six before overstepping, which handed Pakistan a free hit that went for four more. By the end of the second over, Pakistan were 59 without loss, and India needed something close to a miracle to stay in the match.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Abdul Samad hit a six to end the third over, and Pakistan reached 73 for one. In the fourth over, Tewatia was hit for two sixes, and after Khawaja Nafay fell while trying to finish the game, Irfan Khan sealed the victory on the next ball.
 The result was important for Pakistan, who had lost their opening game by a single wicket against the UAE earlier in the day and were close to elimination.
 The tournament will end in three days, with each group winner moving into the semifinals, and the final will be held at Mission Road Ground in Mong Kok on November 1.

 Why the India-Pakistan handshake row has outlasted the result
 Few results in cricket are as predictable as the lack of a handshake between these two sides, and what stands out in Hong Kong is how quickly the gesture, or rather the lack of it, has become routine. Even in a format designed purely for fun, the two captains behaved exactly as their senior teams have done in recent years.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The consistency of the stance is worth noting. India did the same thing in victory in 2025 as in defeat in 2026, which makes it difficult to argue that the gesture is a reaction to results. Whatever one thinks of the policy, it clearly comes from decisions taken above the players, and the captains are simply following them.
 Still, there is a cost. Handshakes are among the few symbols that connect the cricket field to the idea of fair play, and their absence leaves fans with a lingering sense of distance, even when the cricket itself is thrilling. Afridi's five sixes deserved to be remembered for their power, yet the story was shared with a missing greeting.
 Cricket cannot fix diplomacy, but it can make the awkwardness easier to bear by keeping the focus on the contest. That is what the players owe supporters, and for now the bat has done the talking.
